goal.en: Make a good first impression on a new hotel client.
goal.zh: 在新的飯店客戶面前留下好的第一印象。

background: elegant hotel executive office with a wide window overlooking a harbor, polished wooden desk, two leather armchairs, potted orchid, warm pendant lights, soft morning sunlight

intro.en: Your first real client visit. Ms. Wong has brought you to the Harborview Hotel, which wants to upgrade its lighting.
intro.zh: 你的第一次正式客戶拜訪。王經理帶你來到港景飯店，這家飯店正打算更新照明設備。

intro.en: Relax, Kai. Be warm, be brief, and let the client lead at first.
intro.zh: 放輕鬆，凱。親切、簡潔，一開始先讓客戶主導。

intro.en: The office door opens, and the hotel's operations director walks in.
intro.zh: 辦公室的門打開，飯店的營運總監走了進來。

lines.en: Good morning! Ms. Wong, lovely to see you again. And you must be Kai.
lines.zh: 早安！王經理，很高興又見面了。這位一定就是凱吧。

choices.en: Yes, I'm Kai. Thank you for taking the time to meet with us today.
choices.zh: 是的，我是凱。謝謝您今天撥空和我們見面。
choices.tip: Thank you for taking the time to meet. 是拜訪客戶的標準開場，先感謝對方撥出時間。

choices.en: Yes, I'm Kai. Sorry to disturb you, and thank you for your precious time.
choices.zh: 是的，我是凱。打擾了，謝謝您寶貴的時間。

lines.en: Disturb me? Not at all, I invited you. Did I miss something?
lines.zh: 打擾我？完全不會，是我邀請你們來的。我漏掉什麼了嗎？

story.en: Ms. Grant spends the first minute assuring you that you are no bother at all. The meeting starts on a slightly awkward note.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監花了第一分鐘向你保證你完全沒有打擾到她。會議就在有點尷尬的氣氛中開始。

fail.why: 「打擾了」是中文客套話，直譯成 Sorry to disturb you. 會讓對方以為你打斷了什麼；precious time 也太誇張。被邀請來開會時，說 Thank you for taking the time to meet with us. 就很得體。

choices.en: Yep, that's me! Let's skip the small talk and jump straight to prices.
choices.zh: 對，就是我！我們跳過閒聊，直接談價格吧。

lines.en: Straight to prices? I haven't even offered you a coffee yet.
lines.zh: 直接談價格？我連咖啡都還沒請你喝呢。

story.en: Ms. Grant's smile cools by a few degrees. Ms. Wong spends the next ten minutes warming the room back up.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監的笑容降了好幾度。王經理花了十分鐘才把氣氛重新炒熱。

fail.why: 第一次見客戶就說「跳過閒聊、直接談價格」，聽起來急躁又不尊重對方。先道謝、寒暄幾句，讓客戶決定何時進入正題：Thank you for taking the time to meet with us.。

lines.en: Ms. Grant takes a business card from a silver holder and offers it to you.
lines.zh: 葛蘭特總監從銀色名片夾裡抽出一張名片遞給你。

lines.en: Here's my card. My direct line is on the back.
lines.zh: 這是我的名片，背面有我的直撥電話。

choices.en: Thank you. And here's mine. Please feel free to call me anytime.
choices.zh: 謝謝。這是我的名片，有需要請隨時打給我。
choices.tip: 收下名片先道謝，再用 Here's mine. 回遞自己的，簡單又得體。

choices.en: Thank you very much. This is my card. Please give me more advice in the future.
choices.zh: 非常感謝。這是我的名片，以後請多多指教。

lines.en: Advice? Oh... on what, exactly? I'm not sure I'm the right person.
lines.zh: 建議？呃……關於什麼？我不確定我是適合的人選。

story.en: Ms. Grant kindly starts giving you career tips. Fifteen minutes later, nobody has mentioned lighting yet.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監好心地開始給你職涯建議。十五分鐘後，還沒有人提到照明。

fail.why: 「請多指教」是中文的客套話，直譯成 Please give me more advice. 會讓對方以為你真的在請教問題。交換名片時說 Here's mine. Please feel free to call me anytime. 就好。

choices.en: Thanks. This is mine card. If any question, you can contact with me.
choices.zh: 謝謝。這是我的名片，有任何問題可以聯絡我。

lines.en: Contact... with you? Sorry, could you say that again?
lines.zh: 聯絡……跟你？抱歉，可以再說一次嗎？

story.en: You repeat yourself twice, and a simple card exchange stretches into an awkward minute. Ms. Wong gently moves things along.
story.zh: 你又重說了兩次，簡單的交換名片變成了尷尬的一分鐘。王經理溫和地把話題接了過去。

fail.why: 所有格要用 my card，不是 mine card；contact 後面直接接受詞，說 contact me，不加 with。完整說法：If you have any questions, please feel free to contact me.。

lines.en: Please, have a seat. Did you find us all right? Harbor Road can be a nightmare in the morning.
lines.zh: 請坐。路上還好找嗎？港口路早上塞起車來很可怕。

choices.en: No trouble at all. We took the waterfront route, and the view was lovely.
choices.zh: 一點都不麻煩。我們走海濱那條路，風景很美。
choices.tip: 破冰閒聊時給簡短正面的回答，再補一句小細節，話題就能自然延續。

choices.en: It was easy. Wow, you look so young for a director. How old are you?
choices.zh: 很好找。哇，您當總監看起來好年輕，請問您幾歲？

lines.en: Oh! Well... old enough to know not to answer that.
lines.zh: 噢！這個嘛……老到知道不該回答這個問題。

story.en: Ms. Grant laughs it off, but the room goes quiet for a second too long. Ms. Wong quickly asks about the hotel's new restaurant.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監一笑帶過，但現場安靜了好一下。王經理趕緊把話題轉到飯店新開的餐廳。

fail.why: 在台灣稱讚「看起來好年輕」再問年齡很常見，但在西方商務場合，年齡、薪水、婚姻都屬於私人話題。閒聊就聊交通、天氣或城市：No trouble at all. The view was lovely.。

choices.en: Yes. Brightway was founded in 2015, and we now serve over two hundred clients.
choices.zh: 有的。Brightway 成立於 2015 年，目前服務超過兩百家客戶。

lines.en: That's... impressive. I was only asking about the traffic, though.
lines.zh: 這……很厲害。不過我只是在問交通狀況。

story.en: Your answer sounds like a memorized brochure. Ms. Grant checks her watch for the first time.
story.zh: 你的回答聽起來像背好的公司簡介。葛蘭特總監第一次看了手錶。

fail.why: 對方問 Did you find us all right? 是破冰閒聊，不是要聽公司簡介。輕鬆回應交通狀況就好：No trouble at all. We took the waterfront route.。

lines.en: Now, before we start, can I get you anything? Coffee, tea, sparkling water?
lines.zh: 那麼，開始之前，要喝點什麼嗎？咖啡、茶，還是氣泡水？

choices.en: A coffee would be lovely, thank you. Black is fine.
choices.zh: 來杯咖啡就太好了，謝謝。黑咖啡就可以。
choices.tip: would be lovely 是接受招待的得體說法，順便說清楚喜好，對方比較好準備。

choices.en: Give me a black coffee, no sugar. And some water too, please.
choices.zh: 給我一杯黑咖啡，不加糖。也給我一些水。

lines.en: ...Of course. I'll let my assistant know.

story.en: You get your coffee, along with the feeling that you just ordered from a client like a waiter. Ms. Wong raises an eyebrow.
story.zh: 你拿到了咖啡，卻也感覺自己剛剛把客戶當成服務生在點餐。王經理挑了一下眉。

fail.why: Give me... 是命令語氣，對招待你的客戶說會顯得不禮貌，加了 please 也救不太回來。接受招待時說 A coffee would be lovely, thank you. 或 Could I have a coffee, please?。

choices.en: No, no, please don't trouble yourself. Really, we're fine, no need at all.
choices.zh: 不用不用，別麻煩了。真的，我們沒關係，完全不用。

lines.en: Oh. All right, if you're sure.
lines.zh: 喔，好吧，如果你確定的話。

story.en: Ms. Grant takes you at your word. You spend the next hour with a dry throat, watching her sip a fresh cappuccino.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監照字面理解了你的話。接下來一小時，你口乾舌燥地看著她啜飲現煮的卡布奇諾。

fail.why: 在台灣先推辭幾次是禮貌，但在西方，對方通常會照字面接受你的「不用了」。想喝就直接接受：A coffee would be lovely, thank you.；不想喝就說 I'm fine, thank you.。

lines.en: So, I have about thirty minutes before my next meeting. Where would you like to begin?
lines.zh: 我下一個會議前大約有三十分鐘。你們想從哪裡開始？

choices.en: Perhaps you could tell us what you'd like the new lighting to do for your guests.
choices.zh: 或許您可以先告訴我們，您希望新照明為房客帶來什麼。
choices.tip: 先請客戶說出需求，展現傾聽的態度，比急著推銷更有說服力。

choices.en: First we want to know what is your problem with the lighting now.
choices.zh: 我們想先知道你們現在的照明有什麼問題。

lines.en: Our problem? I wasn't aware we had one.
lines.zh: 我們的問題？我倒不知道我們有問題。

story.en: Ms. Grant spends the next ten minutes defending her lobby. Ms. Wong steers the meeting back on course.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監花了十分鐘替她的大廳辯護。王經理把會議拉回正軌。

fail.why: 間接問句要用直述語序：what your problem is，不是 what is your problem；而且直接說客戶「有問題」也容易冒犯人。改說 Could you tell us what you'd like the new lighting to do? 比較好。

choices.en: Thirty minutes is too short for us. Our presentation needs at least an hour.
choices.zh: 三十分鐘對我們來說太短了，我們的簡報至少需要一小時。

lines.en: Then perhaps we should reschedule for when I have an hour.
lines.zh: 那或許我們該改到我有一小時的時候再談。

story.en: Ms. Grant's assistant finds you a new slot... in five weeks. Ms. Wong sighs all the way back to the office.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監的助理幫你們找到新的時段……在五週後。王經理一路嘆氣回到公司。

fail.why: 客戶給你多少時間，就在那段時間內做好，直接說「太短了」等於要求對方配合你。可以說 Thirty minutes is perfect. Perhaps you could start by telling us what you need.。

lines.en: I appreciate a team that listens first. Let's set up a site walkthrough next week.
lines.zh: 我很欣賞先聆聽的團隊。我們下週安排一次實地勘查吧。

lines.en: We'd be delighted. Thank you again, Ms. Grant.
lines.zh: 我們很樂意。再次謝謝您，葛蘭特總監。

story.en: Ms. Grant walks you to the lobby herself. On the way out, Ms. Wong gives you a small nod: your first client visit went well.
story.zh: 葛蘭特總監親自送你們到大廳。離開時，王經理對你輕輕點頭：你的第一次客戶拜訪很成功。

notes.en: Thank you for taking the time to meet.
notes.explain: 拜訪客戶的標準開場白，感謝對方撥出時間給你。比 Thank you for your precious time. 自然得多。

example.en: Thank you for taking the time to meet with us today.
example.zh: 謝謝您今天撥空和我們見面。

notes.en: Sorry to disturb you. / Please give me more advice.
notes.explain: 這兩句都是中文客套話的直譯。disturb 是「干擾」，advice 是真的「建議」，英文母語者會照字面理解。見面說 Thanks for having us.，交換名片說 Here's mine.。

example.en: Thanks for having us. Here's my card.
example.zh: 謝謝邀請我們來，這是我的名片。

notes.en: Please feel free to call me anytime.
notes.explain: 交換名片時的實用結尾句。feel free to + 原形動詞 表示「請別客氣，儘管……」，語氣友善又專業。

example.en: Please feel free to email me if you have any questions.
example.zh: 有任何問題，歡迎隨時寄信給我。

notes.explain: 西方商務會面通常先聊幾句交通、天氣或城市，再進入正題。年齡、薪水、婚姻屬於私人話題，第一次見面不要問。

example.en: Any trouble finding us? Not at all, the directions were great.
example.zh: 路上好找嗎？很好找，路線說明很清楚。

notes.explain: 接受招待時用 would be lovely 很得體。西方人通常會照字面理解你的「不用了」，想喝就一次接受，不必推辭好幾次。

example.en: Tea would be lovely, thank you. No sugar, please.
example.zh: 來杯茶就太好了，謝謝。請不要加糖。
